title: Vertical evaluation commutes with inverse image
statement: For a continuous F:C→D, the product functor on ringed sequence sites and its component at n have module pullbacks adjoint to continuous pushforward. Suppose the ring square commutes and its direct-image evaluation comparison is the identity on sections. Then the inverse mate of that comparison is an isomorphism. Prescribed equalities identifying the evaluated rings may be used. The coefficient and module universe is max(r,c,v), independently of the underlying site universe. The ringed sequence site is [def-coef-ringed-sequence-site].

source.place: Zheng, section 4.1: evaluation and inverse image of coefficient systems

proof.text: Construct the right adjoint to evaluation: at m its sections are the product over proofs n≤m of the evaluated module, with scalars restricted along the horizontal ring map. Vertical sheaf gluing works in each product coordinate. The evaluation and coextension maps give the adjunction.

The continuous direct-image comparison with evaluation is the identity on sections; module pushforward composition constructs it from the commuting ring square. The corresponding coextension mate is an isomorphism, checked coordinatewise. Iterated mates identify it with the conjugate of the inverse-image evaluation mate, hence the latter is invertible. Substitute any prescribed evaluated-ring equalities.

theorem inverseMateFor_isIso
    {D : Type c} [Category.{v} D]
    (J : GrothendieckTopology C) (K : GrothendieckTopology D)
    (F : C ⥤ D) [F.IsContinuous J K]
    [((𝟭 ℕ).prod F).IsContinuous (coefficientSequenceTopology J)
      (coefficientSequenceTopology K)]
    (A : Sheaf (coefficientSequenceTopology J) RingCat.{max r c v})
    (B : Sheaf (coefficientSequenceTopology K) RingCat.{max r c v}) (n : ℕ)
    (φ : A ⟶ (((𝟭 ℕ).prod F).sheafPushforwardContinuous RingCat.{max r c v}
      (coefficientSequenceTopology J) (coefficientSequenceTopology K)).obj B)
    (S : Sheaf J RingCat.{max r c v}) (T : Sheaf K RingCat.{max r c v})
    (hS : ((Prod.sectR n C).sheafPushforwardContinuous RingCat.{max r c v} J
      (coefficientSequenceTopology J)).obj A = S)
    (hT : ((Prod.sectR n D).sheafPushforwardContinuous RingCat.{max r c v} K
      (coefficientSequenceTopology K)).obj B = T)
    (ψ : S ⟶ (F.sheafPushforwardContinuous RingCat.{max r c v} J K).obj T)
    (L : SheafOfModules.{max r c v} A ⥤ SheafOfModules.{max r c v} B)
    (adj : L ⊣ SheafOfModules.pushforward.{max r c v} φ)
    (Ln : SheafOfModules.{max r c v} S ⥤ SheafOfModules.{max r c v} T)
    (adjn : Ln ⊣ SheafOfModules.pushforward.{max r c v} ψ)
    (e : SheafOfModules.pushforward.{max r c v} φ ⋙
        SheafOfModules.pushforward.{max r c v} (F := Prod.sectR n C) (eqToHom hS.symm) ≅
      SheafOfModules.pushforward.{max r c v} (F := Prod.sectR n D) (eqToHom hT.symm) ⋙
        SheafOfModules.pushforward.{max r c v} ψ)
    (he : ∀ (N : SheafOfModules.{max r c v} B) (U : C)
        (x : ((SheafOfModules.pushforward.{max r c v} φ).obj N).val.obj (op (n, U))),
      (e.hom.app N).val.app (op U) x = x) :
    IsIso ((mateEquiv adj adjn).symm e.hom).natTrans
